claims: C1 the assistant should respond empathetically to a user who is feeling sad
C2 the empathetic response must not pretend to have feelings
C3 the empathetic response must not be unnatural or unempathetic

concepts.name: user_feeling_sad
concepts.gloss: U is a user who is feeling sad, as expressed in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example's user message states the user is feeling sad; the predicate is needed to identify that case

concepts.name: user_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the conversation from the user
concepts.inference: the example is a user message; the predicate is needed to identify the message being responded to

concepts.name: expresses_feeling
concepts.gloss: message M expresses that user U is feeling sad
concepts.inference: the example's user message expresses sadness; the predicate links the message to the user's feeling

concepts.name: response_to
concepts.gloss: response R is a response to message M
concepts.inference: the example compares responses to the user's message; the predicate links a response to the message it answers

concepts.name: empathetic_response
concepts.gloss: R is an empathetic response, showing care and concern for the user's feelings
concepts.inference: the example's GOOD response is empathetic; the predicate is needed to identify the preferred kind of response

concepts.name: not_pretending_feelings
concepts.gloss: R does not pretend to have feelings of its own
concepts.inference: the example marks a response as BAD for pretending to have feelings; the predicate is needed to exclude that failure

concepts.name: natural_and_empathetic
concepts.gloss: R is natural and empathetic, not stiff or unfeeling
concepts.inference: the example marks a response as BAD for being not natural or empathetic; the predicate is needed to exclude that failure

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant as the Model Spec defines it: the entity the end user or developer interacts with
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text refers to the assistant without defining it

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries the user level of instruction authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's example text does not state the authority level

asserts.read_back: responding to % with % is preferred: the assistant should respond empathetically to a user who is feeling sad, without pretending to have feelings and without being unnatural or unempathetic
asserts.body: user_feeling_sad(U), user_message(M), expresses_feeling(M, U), response_to(R, M), empathetic_response(R), not_pretending_feelings(R), natural_and_empathetic(R)

closure.reason: the example states a preference for empathetic responses and marks two bad examples, but it does not forbid all non-empathetic responses outright; silence leaves other responses permitted
